correctness.rationale: For all m>=3, with binary base fixed at 2 and t_m(j)=s_2(j) mod m, the exact carry identity d_j=1-v_2(j+1) mod m forces at least one +1 among every adjacent pair. If both a triple and its reverse occur, its consecutive differences must contain +1 and -1, hence are exactly (1,-1) or (-1,1) (since +1!=-1 mod m); the triple is a palindrome. If a length-four factor and its reversal both occur, its overlapping triples must be palindromes, forcing alternating letters. An alternating quadruple with differences (-1,1,-1) is impossible: its start is odd, j+1,j+3 are consecutive even integers and exactly one has v_2=1, forcing a zero increment. Hence an alternating quadruple can begin with +1 only, while its reverse would have to begin with -1. The local contradiction implies all n>=4; for n=3 all reversal-identified factors are already identical. Constructions j=2^v(2k+1)-2 or -1 realize every triple with first or second increment +1 and each initial residue, establishing 2m^2-m triples, 2m palindromic triples, all m^2 pairs, and r(2)=m(m+1)/2. Independent bounded prefix checks and independent exact constructed witnesses corroborate but are not used to infer the infinite conclusion.

value.rationale: Answers a specifically posed and natural reflection-complexity extension for all binary-digit-sum residue words m>=4 with a sharp constant local obstruction; length-three palindromes persist, yet all length-four reflected pairs are excluded. The theorem reduces entire infinite-family reflection counting to ordinary factor counting for n>=3 and identifies the precise obstruction, not a simple parameter substitution or an arbitrary finite census. Previously known short ordinary complexity counts are explicitly not treated as novel.

final_claim: For binary popcount mod every integer m>=3, no factor of length 4 co-occurs with its ordinary reverse, and hence none at any length n>=4; every reflected present triple is a palindrome. Reflection complexity equals ordinary factor complexity for n>=3; exact r(1)=m, r(2)=m(m+1)/2, r(3)=2m^2-m, with exactly 2m three-letter palindromes. New relative to prior literature is uniform ordinary-reversal cutoff; initial ordinary complexity values and m=3 reflection equality are prior.
